title: Data Quality Exploration
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of data quality exploration and identify its main inputs, outputs or constraints.
Apply missingness profiles in a minimal example and state the expected result before checking it.
Test one relevant edge, missing or failure case and describe a limitation of the result.

content.intro: Data Quality Exploration is part of Exploratory Data Analysis and Descriptive Statistics. Start with missingness profiles and connect it to the worked example and expected result.
content.why_it_matters: Data transformations should be explicit and auditable: define the rule, check row counts and keys, and preserve the reason for each cleaning choice.

content_blocks.title: Why this matters
content_blocks.text: Data transformations should be explicit and auditable: define the rule, check row counts and keys, and preserve the reason for each cleaning choice. The example is intentionally small so you can predict its result before checking it in a local R session.

content_blocks.title: Work through it
content_blocks.text: Compare before/after row counts, check a key or range invariant, and record how missing or duplicate records were handled. Change one input or condition at a time, compare the observed result with your prediction, and write down one limitation.

content_blocks.title: R example: Data Quality Exploration
content_blocks.code:
# Lesson 134: Data Quality Exploration
example_rows <- data.frame(group = c("A", "B", "A"), amount = c(3, 4, 5))
aggregate(amount ~ group, data = example_rows, sum)
content_blocks.run_instructions: CodeLeaf does not provide an R runtime. This block is an inspectable reference example; execute it in a local R console or a reviewed R-aware environment. Static validation checks file structure, not R semantics.
content_blocks.reset_steps: No example is executed by this CodeLeaf lesson. For a local run, use synthetic data in a temporary working directory, avoid production credentials or destructive writes, and restart a clean R session to clear lesson objects.
content_blocks.limitations: Synthetic grouping demonstrates a transformation; validate key relationships and row counts in a real workflow. Verify the snippet and expected output with the supported R and package versions before publishing.

content_blocks.title: Common pitfall
content_blocks.text: Do not treat a syntactically plausible example as proof of correctness. For data quality exploration, check the input type, missing/empty cases, output shape, and domain assumptions.

common_mistakes.problem: Using an example without checking its inputs or output shape.
common_mistakes.why: R can coerce types, propagate missing values or simplify results unexpectedly.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect with str(), class(), typeof(), length() or dim() and add a direct check.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating a demonstration as proof that every edge case works.
common_mistakes.why: Empty input, missing values, dependencies and version differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Test a normal case and a boundary/failure case in a clean local R session.

common_mistakes.why: The conclusion depends on data provenance, transformations and assumptions.
common_mistakes.fix: Record input source, cleaning choices and known limitations beside the result.
